title: What Will Be The Pivot Point For Policy?
gist: Gavekal Dragonomics teaser (Batson): China will claim to have hit its 4.5–5% 2026 GDP target thanks to surging exports, but real domestic demand growth is below 3% — as weak as in 2024 before the much-publicized 'policy pivot', which changed little; Beijing keeps tinkering with just-enough stimulus because the costs haven't yet forced a change of course.

insights.claim: China is set to declare it met its 2026 GDP growth target of 4.5–5%, a result mainly due to another stunning rise in exports rather than domestic strength.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: China's headline growth is export-dependent — a source of trade friction and deflation export to the rest of the world.
insights.locator: The government is again preparing to declare

insights.claim: Real growth in China's domestic demand is running below 3% in 2026, similar to the pace in 2024 when the government announced its much-publicized policy pivot to support growth.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Domestic consumption-linked China plays remain unsupported; demand weakness is persistent, not cyclical.
insights.quote: Real growth in domestic demand, though, is now running at less than 3%

insights.claim: China's government's 2024 'policy pivot' did not materially change policy: the government has kept tinkering at the margins, providing just enough stimulus to meet its growth target while domestic demand stays weak.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Fade announcements of Chinese stimulus 'pivots' unless accompanied by a real change in scale or direction.
insights.locator: But actual policy ultimately did not change much

insights.claim: The costs of China's weak-demand, export-led dynamic have apparently not been large enough to push the leadership onto a different policy course — implying a real pivot requires a bigger pain point.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Look for the trigger (export shock, financial stress, unemployment) that would raise the cost enough to force genuine stimulus.
insights.locator: This dynamic persisted despite its costs
